docs.title: OpenLeaf
docs.text: Open-source aviation sustainability suite — aircraft performance modeling and trajectory optimization.

docs.title: Quick Install
docs.text:
Bash
uv add openleaf-performance

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
Python
import numpy as np
from openleaf.performance.core import ModelFactory, TrajectoryData

# Load an aircraft model (OpenAP requires no configuration)
model = ModelFactory.load("A320", model_type="openap")

# Build a trajectory
traj = TrajectoryData({
    "altitude": np.array([10000.0, 10500.0]),
    "true_airspeed": np.array([230.0, 232.0]),
    "vertical_speed": np.array([5.0, 5.0]),
    "aircraft_mass": np.array([65000.0, 64900.0]),
    "acceleration": np.array([0.1, 0.1]),
})

# Attach model and compute performance
perf = traj.with_aircraft(model)
print(perf.drag)       # Aerodynamic drag [N]
print(perf.thrust)     # Required thrust [N]
print(perf.fuel_flow)  # Fuel flow rate [kg/s]

docs.title: openleaf-performance
docs.text:
Modular, differentiable aircraft performance models for trajectory optimization

openleaf-performance provides aircraft performance models (BADA3, BADA4, OpenAP, Poll-Schumann) behind a unified interface. All models support NumPy arrays and CasADi symbolic types, making them suitable for both analysis and trajectory optimization.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Bash
uv add openleaf-performance

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
Python
import numpy as np
from openleaf.performance.core import ModelFactory, TrajectoryData

# Load an aircraft model (OpenAP requires no configuration)
model = ModelFactory.load("A320", model_type="openap")

# Build a trajectory
traj = TrajectoryData({
    "altitude": np.array([10000.0, 10500.0]),       # Pressure altitude [m]
    "true_airspeed": np.array([230.0, 232.0]),       # TAS [m/s]
    "vertical_speed": np.array([5.0, 5.0]),          # dHp/dt [m/s]
    "aircraft_mass": np.array([65000.0, 64900.0]),   # [kg]
    "acceleration": np.array([0.1, 0.1]),            # dV/dt [m/s^2]
})

# Attach model and compute performance
perf = traj.with_aircraft(model)
print(perf.drag)       # Aerodynamic drag [N]
print(perf.thrust)     # Required thrust [N]
print(perf.fuel_flow)  # Fuel flow rate [kg/s]

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 4 performance models -- BADA3, BADA4, OpenAP, and Poll-Schumann
  • Multi-backend dispatch -- NumPy, JAX, CasADi, and PyTorch via a unified array API
  • Lazy trajectory container -- automatic ISA, airspeed conversions, energy share factor
  • Flight envelope checking -- configurable violation modes (ignore, warn, raise)
  • Unified factory -- load any model by ICAO code with ModelFactory.load()

docs.title: Core (core/)
docs.text:
Defines the interfaces and containers that all model implementations share:

  • AircraftModel -- abstract base class composed of three subsystems: EngineModel (thrust, fuel flow), AerodynamicsModel (drag coefficient), and LimitsModel (flight envelope). Every backend implements these.
  • TrajectoryData -- lazy container for flight state arrays (altitude, TAS, vertical speed, mass). Automatically derives ISA properties, Mach, CAS, and energy share factor on first access. All properties are cached.
  • AircraftTrajectoryData -- extends TrajectoryData with an attached aircraft model. Adds computed performance (drag, thrust, fuel flow) via FlightStateMixin and PerformanceMixin.
  • EnvelopeChecker -- validates flight state against aircraft limits (overspeed, underspeed, ceiling, mass). Configurable modes: IGNORE, WARN, RAISE.
  • ModelFactory -- unified entry point that loads any model by ICAO code. Tries model types in priority order (BADA4 > BADA3 > OpenAP > PS).

docs.title: Models (models/)
docs.text:
Four concrete implementations of AircraftModel:

Backend Data source Parsing Strengths BADA3 .OPF files (EUROCONTROL) Regex extraction Wide aircraft coverage, simple coefficients BADA4 XML files (EUROCONTROL) ElementTree High-fidelity polynomials, configuration-dependent OpenAP openap Python library Library wrapper Open data, no license required PS pycontrails library Library wrapper Contrail/climate research, Reynolds-based drag

All backends share a common pattern:

  1. Pydantic schemas -- frozen data classes for aircraft, engine, aero, limits
  2. Parsing -- format-specific (regex, XML, library API)
  3. Synonym resolution -- maps ICAO codes to data files
  4. Configuration selection -- shared logic in models/common/ determines aerodynamic configuration (cruise, climb, approach, landing) from altitude, speed, and flight phase

docs.title: Physics (physics/)
docs.text:
Domain modules used by models and trajectory calculations:

  • isa -- International Standard Atmosphere (temperature, pressure, density from altitude). Provides AtmosphericState with cached properties.
  • aero -- Aerodynamic calculations (dynamic pressure, drag, thrust required). AircraftAirspeed converts between TAS, CAS, and Mach.
  • esf -- Energy share factor for different speed schedules (constant CAS, constant Mach, acceleration/deceleration).
  • tem -- Total Energy Model (BADA equation 3.1-1). Computes rate of climb/descent from thrust and drag balance.
  • units -- SI constants and conversions (knots, feet, nautical miles).

docs.title: Numpy dispatch (numpy/)
docs.text: A thin abstraction layer that routes array operations to the correct backend based on input type. See Multi-backend dispatch for details.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Rationale CasADi-first dispatch Trajectory optimization requires symbolic differentiation. CasADi types are checked first because they cannot go through the Array API path. Array API for non-CasADi NumPy, JAX, and PyTorch all support the Python Array API standard, so a single code path handles all three. Lazy trajectory properties Flight state quantities are expensive to compute and not always needed. cached_property avoids redundant work. Pydantic frozen models Aircraft data is immutable after parsing. Frozen models prevent accidental mutation and enable hashing. Mixin composition FlightStateMixin and PerformanceMixin separate flight state derivation from performance computation, keeping TrajectoryData focused. Common config selection Aerodynamic configuration logic (clean, takeoff, approach, landing) is shared across BADA3/BADA4/PS in models/common/, avoiding duplication.

docs.title: Multi-backend dispatch
docs.text: openleaf-performance supports four array backends through a unified dispatch layer in the numpy/ module. Code written against this layer works unchanged with any supported backend.

docs.title: Supported backends
docs.text: Backend Import Use case NumPy numpy General analysis, data processing CasADi casadi Trajectory optimization (symbolic AD) JAX jax.numpy GPU acceleration, JIT compilation PyTorch torch GPU acceleration, ML integration

docs.title: How dispatch works
docs.text:
Every math function in openleaf.performance.numpy (e.g., sqrt, where, sin, clip) follows the same two-step dispatch:

  1. CasADi check first. If any input is a CasADi type (MX, DM, or SX), the function delegates to the corresponding casadi method. This check happens first because CasADi types do not implement the Python Array API.

  2. Array API fallback. For all other types, get_array_namespace(*arrays) (from array-api-compat) returns the correct namespace (numpy, jax.numpy, torch), and the function calls the standard method on that namespace.

Text Only
Input arrays
    |
    +-- is_casadi_type? --> casadi.sqrt, casadi.if_else, ...
    |
    +-- else --> get_array_namespace() --> xp.sqrt, xp.where, ...
                    |
                    +-- numpy.ndarray   --> numpy
                    +-- jax.Array       --> jax.numpy
                    +-- torch.Tensor    --> torch
                    +-- int/float       --> numpy (default)

docs.title: CasADi specifics
docs.text:
CasADi is the primary optimization backend. Its symbolic types (MX for optimization variables, DM for dense matrices, SX for scalar expressions) require special handling:

  • No boolean indexing. Use np.where(condition, a, b) instead of a[mask].
  • No shape inspection at build time. Symbolic dimensions are resolved at solve time.
  • Interpolation. interpn with CasADi inputs uses CasADi's built-in B-spline or linear interpolation instead of SciPy.

Because all physics and model code uses openleaf.performance.numpy as a drop-in replacement for NumPy, switching to CasADi requires no code changes in the model layer -- only the input types change.

docs.title: When to use which backend
docs.text: Scenario Backend Why Batch analysis of flight data NumPy Fast, no dependencies beyond NumPy Trajectory optimization (NLP) CasADi Symbolic automatic differentiation for NLP solvers Large-scale GPU computation JAX or PyTorch Hardware acceleration, JIT compilation ML pipeline integration PyTorch Native tensor interop with PyTorch models

docs.title: Interpolation dispatch
docs.text:
The interpn function has its own dispatch logic because interpolation methods differ significantly between backends:

Input type Method Backend used NumPy linear, nearest SciPy (direct delegation) NumPy bspline CasADi (SciPy has no B-spline interpn) CasADi linear, bspline CasADi native interpolation

See Interpolation reference for the full API.

docs.title: Performance models
docs.text: openleaf-performance implements four aircraft performance models. All share the same AircraftModel interface (engine, aerodynamics, limits subsystems) but differ in data source, fidelity, and licensing.

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: BADA3 BADA4 OpenAP Poll-Schumann Source EUROCONTROL EUROCONTROL Open data (TU Delft) pycontrails (Contrails.org) License Proprietary Proprietary Open Open Data format .OPF text files XML files Python library Python library Aircraft coverage ~400 types ~150 types ~100 types ~80 types Fidelity Medium High Medium Medium (cruise focus) Configurations 5 (CR, IC, TO, AP, LD) Config-dependent (HLid + LG) Flap angle + gear Clean only Flight phases All All All Cruise

docs.title: BADA3
docs.text:
Base of Aircraft Data version 3, the most widely used model in ATM research.

  • Data: OPF files parsed via regex, one file per aircraft type
  • Engine model: Polynomial thrust coefficients (5 for max thrust, 4 for fuel flow). Thrust depends on altitude; fuel flow depends on TAS.
  • Aerodynamics: Drag polars (CD0, CD2) per aerodynamic configuration. Stall speeds are mass-corrected using sqrt(m/m_ref).
  • Envelope: VMO/MMO/HMO limits. Maximum altitude is mass- and temperature-dependent (formula 3.5-1). Buffet onset via CLbo coefficient.
  • Synonyms: SYNONYM.NEW file maps ICAO codes to OPF file prefixes.

docs.title: BADA4
docs.text:
Version 4 replaces simple coefficients with high-order polynomials evaluated over (delta, Mach) domains.

  • Data: XML files with structured element trees, one folder per aircraft
  • Engine model: Bivariate polynomials for thrust as a function of pressure ratio (delta) and Mach number. Separate coefficient sets for different engine settings (MCMB, MCRZ, LIDL, etc.).
  • Aerodynamics: Drag coefficients indexed by (high-lift device position, landing gear state). Supports ARPM (Airline Procedure Model) configuration.
  • Envelope: Geometric, kinematic, and buffet limit models (GLM/KLM/BLM). Configuration-dependent VFE and CL_max.
  • Synonyms: SYNONYM.BD4 file maps ICAO codes to XML folder names.

docs.title: OpenAP
docs.text:
Open Aircraft Performance model based on publicly available data.

  • Data: Loaded via the openap Python library (no file parsing)
  • Engine model: Simplified thrust and fuel flow functions from the OpenAP database.
  • Aerodynamics: Drag polar with configuration selection via flap angle and landing gear flags (rather than the altitude/speed thresholds used by BADA).
  • Envelope: Constant VMO, MMO, HMO (service ceiling). No configuration-dependent adjustments.
  • Synonyms: Uses OpenAP's built-in synonym dictionary.

OpenAP is the easiest model to get started with -- it requires no license or data configuration.

docs.title: Poll-Schumann (PS)
docs.text:
A cruise-focused model designed for contrail and climate impact research.

  • Data: Loaded via the pycontrails library
  • Engine model: Thrust and efficiency coefficients with idle fuel flow parameters. Designed for cruise conditions.
  • Aerodynamics: Reynolds-based skin friction drag plus wave drag (coefficients j1, j2, j3) and induced drag via Oswald efficiency factor. Wing aspect ratio is computed from span and area.
  • Envelope: Altitude-dependent Mach limits derived from impact pressure constraints (p_i_max). VMO is effectively infinite (Mach limits dominate at cruise altitudes).
  • Limitations: Clean configuration only; not suitable for climb/descent with deployed high-lift devices.

docs.title: Choosing a model
docs.text:
• Need open data with no setup? Use OpenAP.
  • Need high fidelity for all flight phases? Use BADA4 (requires license).
  • Need wide aircraft coverage? Use BADA3 (requires license).
  • Working on contrail/climate research? Use Poll-Schumann.
  • Not sure? Use ModelFactory.load("A320") -- it picks the best available.

docs.title: How-To Guides
docs.text: Task-oriented guides for common workflows.

docs.title: Available guides
docs.text:
• Resolve an aircraft code -- map an ICAO type code to a performance model using the synonym system
  • Switch backend -- use CasADi, JAX, or PyTorch instead of NumPy for optimization or GPU acceleration

docs.title: Resolve an aircraft code
docs.text: This guide shows how to find which performance models are available for a given ICAO aircraft type code, and how the synonym system maps codes to data files.

docs.title: Check availability across all models
docs.text:
Python
from openleaf.performance.core import ModelFactory

# Check one aircraft across all model types
availability = ModelFactory.is_available("A320")
print(availability)
# {ModelType.BADA3: True, ModelType.BADA4: True, ModelType.OPENAP: True, ModelType.PS: True}

# Check for a specific model type
ModelFactory.is_available("A320", model_type="bada4")
# True

docs.title: List all available aircraft
docs.text:
Python
# All aircraft for a given model type
aircraft_list = ModelFactory.available_aircraft("openap")
print(aircraft_list)
# ['A319', 'A320', 'A321', 'B738', ...]

# All aircraft across all model types
all_aircraft = ModelFactory.available_aircraft()
# {ModelType.BADA3: [...], ModelType.BADA4: [...], ...}

docs.title: How synonym resolution works
docs.text: BADA3 and BADA4 use synonym files to map ICAO codes to data files on disk. This is necessary because data file names do not always match ICAO codes.

docs.title: BADA4 resolution order
docs.text:
1. Look up ICAO code in SYNONYM.BD4 to get a folder name
  2. Search for folder/name.xml in the data directory
  3. Search for any XML file in the folder
  4. Fall back to filesystem scan matching the ICAO prefix

docs.title: BADA3 resolution order
docs.text:
1. Look up ICAO code in SYNONYM.NEW to get an OPF prefix
  2. Try prefix.OPF directly
  3. Try underscore suffix variants (prefix__.OPF, prefix___.OPF, prefix_.OPF)
  4. Fall back to filesystem scan

docs.title: OpenAP and Poll-Schumann
docs.text: These models use their respective library's built-in synonym dictionaries. No file-level resolution is needed.

docs.title: Handle missing aircraft
docs.text:
When an aircraft is not found, ModelFactory.load() raises a ValueError listing all model types it tried:

Python
from openleaf.performance.core import ModelFactory

try:
    model = ModelFactory.load("ZZZZ")
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
    # Aircraft 'ZZZZ' not found in any model. Tried:
    #   - bada4: ...
    #   - bada3: ...
    #   - openap: ...
    #   - ps: ...

To load from a specific file when the synonym system does not cover your aircraft:

Python
model = ModelFactory.load_from_file("/path/to/custom/A320.xml", model_type="bada4")

docs.title: Switch backend
docs.text: By default, openleaf-performance uses NumPy arrays. You can switch to CasADi, JAX, or PyTorch by simply passing different array types as input. No configuration or code changes are needed in the model layer.

docs.title: Use CasADi for trajectory optimization
docs.text:
CasADi enables symbolic automatic differentiation, required by NLP solvers like IPOPT.

Python
import casadi as ca
import numpy as np
from openleaf.performance.core import TrajectoryData
from openleaf.performance.models.openap import OpenAPModel

model = OpenAPModel("A320")
n = 100  # number of trajectory points

# Create CasADi symbolic variables
altitude = ca.MX.sym("altitude", n)
tas = ca.MX.sym("tas", n)
vs = ca.MX.sym("vs", n)
mass = ca.MX.sym("mass", n)
accel = ca.MX.sym("accel", n)

# TrajectoryData works with CasADi MX types unchanged
traj = TrajectoryData({
    "altitude": altitude,
    "true_airspeed": tas,
    "vertical_speed": vs,
    "aircraft_mass": mass,
    "acceleration": accel,
})

perf = traj.with_aircraft(model)

# perf.fuel_flow is now a CasADi symbolic expression
# Use it in an NLP objective or constraint
total_fuel = ca.sum1(perf.fuel_flow)

All internal operations (np.where, np.sqrt, interpolation) automatically dispatch to CasADi equivalents.

docs.title: How dispatch works internally
docs.text:
The dispatch layer in openleaf.performance.numpy checks input types at runtime:

  1. If any input is a CasADi type (MX, DM, SX), use CasADi operations
  2. Otherwise, use array-api-compat to get the correct namespace (NumPy, JAX, or PyTorch)

This means you never need to change model code or configuration. The backend is determined entirely by the types you pass in.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• CasADi: No boolean indexing or shape inspection at build time. All branching must use np.where.
  • JAX: Requires jax and jaxlib installed. JIT compilation adds overhead on first call.
  • PyTorch: Some operations may not support all dtypes (e.g., complex).
  • Interpolation: bspline method always uses CasADi regardless of input type (SciPy has no B-spline interpn).

See Multi-backend dispatch for a deeper explanation of the dispatch architecture.

docs.title: interpn
docs.text:
Python
from openleaf.performance.numpy.interpolate import interpn

Performs multidimensional interpolation on regular grids, analogous to scipy.interpolate.interpn.

Automatically dispatches between a NumPy/SciPy fast path and a CasADi backend depending on input types and method.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
Python
def interpn(
    points: tuple[ndarray],
    values: ndarray,
    xi: ndarray,
    method: Literal["linear", "bspline", "nearest"] = "linear",
    bounds_error: bool = True,
    fill_value: float = nan,
) -> ndarray

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description points tuple[ndarray] Coordinates of each grid axis. Shapes (m1,), ..., (mn,) values ndarray Data on the regular grid. Shape (m1, ..., mn) xi ndarray Coordinates to sample at. Shape (..., ndim) method str "linear", "bspline", or "nearest" bounds_error bool Raise ValueError for out-of-bounds xi (default True) fill_value float \| None Value for out-of-bounds points. None clamps to grid edge

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
• "linear" — Differentiable but C1-discontinuous. Uses SciPy for pure NumPy inputs, CasADi otherwise.
  • "bspline" — Piecewise-cubic, differentiable, suitable for optimization. CasADi only. May overshoot (not monotonicity-preserving).
  • "nearest" — Not differentiable. Uses SciPy fast path only.

docs.title: Backend dispatch
docs.text: xi type method Backend NumPy linear, nearest SciPy (direct delegation) NumPy bspline CasADi CasADi MX/DM linear, bspline CasADi

docs.title: FlightStateMixin
docs.text:
Flight state properties derived from trajectory and aircraft model.

Expects the container class to provide: - _model: an AircraftModel instance - _traj: a dict-like trajectory data store

docs.title: aircraft_mass cached property
docs.text: Aircraft mass [kg].

docs.title: delta_isa cached property
docs.text: Temperature deviation from ISA [K].

docs.title: flight_phase cached property
docs.text:
Flight phase (CLIMB, CRUISE, DESCENT) from vertical speed.

Derived from vertical_speed using standard thresholds: - vs > 0.5 m/s → CLIMB - vs < -0.5 m/s → DESCENT - otherwise → CRUISE

docs.title: aerodynamic_configuration cached property
docs.text:
Aerodynamic configuration (TO, IC, CR, AP, LD) from model.

Configuration depends on flight phase, altitude, and speed. Returns None for models without configuration (e.g., PS cruise-only).

docs.title: high_lift cached property
docs.text:
High-lift device state (hlid) from model.

Model-specific return type: - BADA4: HLid string ("0", "1", etc.) - OpenAP: Flap angle in degrees - BADA3/PS: None

docs.title: landing_gear cached property
docs.text:
Landing gear state from model.

Returns True if gear extended, False if retracted. May return None for models that don't track gear state.

docs.title: engine_setting cached property
docs.text:
Engine setting derived from flight phase.

Maps flight phase to engine setting: - CLIMB → MCMB (Maximum Continuous Climb) - CRUISE → MCRZ (Maximum Continuous Cruise) - DESCENT → LIDL (Idle)

docs.title: PerformanceMixin
docs.text:
Performance properties that delegate to an aircraft model.

Expects the container class to provide: - _model: an AircraftModel instance - _traj: a dict-like trajectory data store - drag, aircraft_mass, f, air_temperature (for the TEM thrust calculation)

docs.title: drag cached property
docs.text: Aerodynamic drag [N].

docs.title: drag_coef cached property
docs.text:
Drag coefficient [-].

Requires aerodynamic_configuration for BADA3/BADA4/OpenAP. PS model uses cruise-only clean configuration.

docs.title: fuel_flow cached property
docs.text: Fuel flow rate [kg/s].

docs.title: fuel_flow_min cached property
docs.text: Minimum fuel flow rate (idle) [kg/s].

docs.title: lift_coef cached property
docs.text: Lift coefficient [-].

docs.title: thrust cached property
docs.text:
Required thrust [N] from Total Energy Model.

Uses the TEM equation to compute thrust given: - drag (from aerodynamic model) - vertical_speed (pressure altitude rate) - energy share factor f

Formula (BADA Manual 3.1-4): T = D + (m · g · dh_geo/dt) / (V · f)

where dh_geo/dt is derived from pressure altitude rate using temperature correction.

docs.title: Synonym Resolution
docs.text: BADA3 and BADA4 backends use synonym files to map ICAO aircraft type codes to data files on disk. The resolution functions handle normalization, synonym lookup, filesystem fallback, and error reporting.

docs.title: BADA4
docs.text:
Resolves an ICAO code to a BADA4 XML file path. Resolution order:

  1. Synonym lookup: folder/name.xml
  2. Synonym lookup: folder/*.xml (any XML in folder)
  3. Synonym lookup: data_path/name.xml (direct file)
  4. Filesystem scan: folders matching ICAO prefix
  5. Filesystem scan: XML files matching ICAO prefix

docs.title: resolve_bada4_file(icao, data_path, synonym_file=None)
docs.text:
Resolve ICAO code to BADA4 XML file path.

Args: icao: ICAO aircraft type code (e.g., 'A320'). data_path: Path to BADA4 data directory. synonym_file: Path to SYNONYM.BD4 file. If None, looks for it in data_path.

Returns: Path to the XML file for this aircraft.

Raises: FileNotFoundError: If aircraft not found in synonyms or XML file doesn't exist.

Source code in packages/openleaf-performance/src/openleaf/performance/models/bada4/synonyms.py Python
def resolve_bada4_file(
    icao: str,
    data_path: Path,
    synonym_file: Path | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Resolve ICAO code to BADA4 XML file path.

    Args:
        icao: ICAO aircraft type code (e.g., 'A320').
        data_path: Path to BADA4 data directory.
        synonym_file: Path to SYNONYM.BD4 file. If None, looks for it in data_path.

    Returns:
        Path to the XML file for this aircraft.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If aircraft not found in synonyms or XML file doesn't exist.
    """
    icao = icao.upper().strip()

    if synonym_file is None:
        synonym_file = data_path / "SYNONYM.BD4"

    if synonym_file.exists():
        result = _resolve_via_synonyms_bada4(icao, _get_synonyms(synonym_file), data_path)
        if result is not None:
            return result

    result = _resolve_fallback_bada4(icao, data_path)
    if result is not None:
        return result

    raise build_not_found_error(icao, "BADA4", data_path, synonym_file, _get_synonyms, "*.xml")

docs.title: BADA3
docs.text:
Resolves an ICAO code to a BADA3 OPF file path. Resolution order:

  1. Synonym lookup: prefix.OPF (exact)
  2. Synonym lookup: prefix with underscore variants (__, ___, _)
  3. Filesystem scan: ICAO + suffix patterns (__, ___, _, empty)

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This tutorial walks you through loading an aircraft model and computing performance quantities (drag, thrust, fuel flow) for a flight trajectory.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • uv (recommended) or pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Bash
uv add openleaf-performance

Or with pip:

Bash
pip install openleaf-performance

docs.title: Step 1: Configure data paths (BADA only)
docs.text:
OpenAP and Poll-Schumann models work out of the box. BADA3 and BADA4 require you to point to the data directories provided by EUROCONTROL:

Python
import openleaf.performance

# Set paths once -- they are persisted in ~/.config/openleaf/settings.toml
openleaf.performance.set_bada4_path("/path/to/bada4/data")
openleaf.performance.set_bada3_path("/path/to/bada3/data")

# Verify configuration
openleaf.performance.show_config()

Skip this step if you only use OpenAP or Poll-Schumann.

docs.title: Step 2: Load an aircraft model
docs.text:
The ModelFactory provides a single entry point for all model types:

Python
from openleaf.performance.core import ModelFactory

# Auto-detect best available model (tries BADA4 > BADA3 > OpenAP > PS)
model = ModelFactory.load("A320")

# Or request a specific model type
model = ModelFactory.load("A320", model_type="openap")
model = ModelFactory.load("B738", model_type="bada4")

You can also instantiate models directly:

Python
from openleaf.performance.models.openap import OpenAPModel

model = OpenAPModel("A320")
print(model.data)      # Aircraft data: model, WTC, engine type
print(model.limits)    # LimitsData: MTOM, VMO, MMO, HMO

docs.title: Step 3: Build a trajectory
docs.text:
TrajectoryData is a lazy container that holds flight state arrays and automatically computes derived quantities (ISA atmosphere, Mach number, calibrated airspeed, energy share factor) on first access.

Python
import numpy as np
from openleaf.performance.core import TrajectoryData

data = {
    "altitude": np.array([10000.0, 10500.0, 11000.0]),       # Pressure altitude Hp [m]
    "true_airspeed": np.array([230.0, 232.0, 234.0]),        # TAS [m/s]
    "vertical_speed": np.array([5.0, 5.0, 0.0]),             # dHp/dt [m/s]
    "aircraft_mass": np.array([65000.0, 64900.0, 64800.0]),  # [kg]
    "acceleration": np.array([0.1, 0.1, 0.0]),               # dV/dt [m/s^2]
}

traj = TrajectoryData(data)

# Derived quantities are computed lazily
print(traj.mach_number)          # Mach from TAS and ISA temperature
print(traj.calibrated_airspeed)  # CAS [m/s]
print(traj.air_temperature)      # ISA temperature [K]
print(traj.air_pressure)         # ISA pressure [Pa]

You can provide either acceleration (dV/dt) or f (energy share factor). The missing one is derived automatically.

docs.title: Step 4: Compute aircraft performance
docs.text:
Attach the aircraft model to the trajectory to compute drag, thrust, and fuel flow:

Python
perf = traj.with_aircraft(model)

# Performance quantities (computed lazily, cached)
print(perf.drag)            # Aerodynamic drag [N]
print(perf.thrust)          # Required thrust [N]
print(perf.fuel_flow)       # Fuel flow [kg/s]
print(perf.drag_coef)       # CD [-]

The with_aircraft method also accepts a string shorthand:

Python
perf = traj.with_aircraft("OpenAP", "A320")
perf = traj.with_aircraft("BADA4", "B738")

docs.title: Step 5: Check the flight envelope
docs.text:
By default, envelope violations are ignored. You can change this behavior:

Python
from openleaf.performance.core import EnvelopeMode

# Warn on violations (logs a warning)
perf = traj.with_aircraft(model, envelope_mode=EnvelopeMode.WARN)

# Raise on violations (raises EnvelopeViolationError)
perf = traj.with_aircraft(model, envelope_mode=EnvelopeMode.RAISE)

Envelope checks cover: overspeed (CAS and Mach), underspeed (stall), ceiling altitude, and mass bounds.

docs.title: performance
docs.text:
OpenLeaf - Aircraft performance models for trajectory optimization.

This package provides aircraft performance models including BADA3, BADA4, OpenAP, and Poll-Schumann models with CasADi-compatible operations for seamless trajectory optimization.

Main modules: - core: Core performance model interfaces and abstract base classes - models: Aircraft model implementations (BADA3, BADA4, OpenAP, PS) - physics: Aerodynamics, ISA atmosphere, and physics utilities - numpy: NumPy-compatible operations supporting CasADi symbolic types - utils: Type definitions and utility functions

Configuration: BADA3 and BADA4 models require configuration of data paths:

Text Only
>>> import openleaf.performance
>>> openleaf.performance.set_bada3_path("/path/to/bada3/data")
>>> openleaf.performance.set_bada4_path("/path/to/bada4/data")
>>> openleaf.performance.show_config()

Usage: >>> from openleaf.performance.models.bada3 import BADA3Model >>> from openleaf.performance.models.bada4 import BADA4Model >>> from openleaf.performance.models.openap import OpenAPModel >>> from openleaf.performance.models.ps import PSModel >>> >>> # All models use the same interface >>> model = BADA3Model("A320") >>> model = OpenAPModel("A320")

Attributes: section: OPF section where error occurred (e.g., "AERO", "FUEL").

Source code in packages/openleaf-performance/src/openleaf/performance/exceptions.py Python
class BADA3ParseError(ParsingError):
    """Raised when BADA3 OPF/APF file parsing fails.

    Attributes:
        section: OPF section where error occurred (e.g., "AERO", "FUEL").
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        filepath: str | None = None,
        section: str | None = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(message, filepath)
        self.section = section

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        base = Exception.__str__(self)
        parts = [base]
        if self.filepath:
            parts.append(f"file: {self.filepath}")
        if self.section:
            parts.append(f"section: {self.section}")
        if len(parts) > 1:
            return f"{parts[0]} ({', '.join(parts[1:])})"
        return base

        field: str,
        method: str | None = None,

class ValueRangeError(ValidationError):
    """Raised when a value is outside its valid range.

    Attributes:
        field: Name of the field with invalid value.
        value: The invalid value.
        min_value: Minimum allowed value (if applicable).
        max_value: Maximum allowed value (if applicable).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        field: str,
        value: float,
        min_value: float | None = None,
        max_value: float | None = None,
        message: str | None = None,
    ):
        if message is None:
            if min_value is not None and max_value is not None:
                message = f"'{field}' value {value} outside range [{min_value}, {max_value}]"
            elif min_value is not None:
                message = f"'{field}' value {value} below minimum {min_value}"
            elif max_value is not None:
                message = f"'{field}' value {value} above maximum {max_value}"
            else:
                message = f"'{field}' value {value} is invalid"
        super().__init__(message)
        self.field = field
        self.value = value
        self.min_value = min_value
        self.max_value = max_value

class OpenLeafSettings(BaseSettings):
    """OpenLeaf configuration.

    Settings are loaded from (highest to lowest priority):
    1. Environment variables (OPENLEAF_BADA3_PATH, OPENLEAF_BADA4_PATH, etc.)
    2. TOML config file (~/.config/openleaf/settings.toml)
    3. Field defaults (None)
    """

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="OPENLEAF_",
        env_nested_delimiter="_",
    )

    bada3: Bada3Settings = Field(default_factory=Bada3Settings)
    bada4: Bada4Settings = Field(default_factory=Bada4Settings)

    @classmethod
    def settings_customise_sources(
        cls,
        settings_cls: type[BaseSettings],
        init_settings: Any,
        env_settings: Any,
        dotenv_settings: Any,
        file_secret_settings: Any,
    ) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
        """Priority: init > env vars > TOML file."""
        toml_path = _get_config_path()
        sources: list[Any] = [init_settings, env_settings]
        if toml_path.exists():
            sources.append(TomlConfigSettingsSource(settings_cls, toml_file=toml_path))
        return tuple(sources)

def get_bada3_path() -> Path:
    """Get the configured BADA3 data path.

    Returns:
        Path to BADA3 data directory.

    Raises:
        ConfigurationError: If BADA3 path is not configured.
    """
    path_str = _get_settings().bada3.path
    if not path_str:
        msg = (
            "BADA3 data path not configured.\n\n"
            "Please set it using:\n"
            "  >>> import openleaf.performance\n"
            "  >>> openleaf.performance.set_bada3_path('/path/to/bada3/data')\n\n"
            "Or set environment variable: OPENLEAF_BADA3_PATH\n\n"
            f"Config file location: {config_path()}"
        )
        raise ConfigurationError(msg)
    path = Path(path_str)
    if not path.exists():
        msg = f"BADA3 data path does not exist: {path}"
        raise ConfigurationError(msg)
    return path

def get_bada3_synonyms_path() -> Path | None:

    s = _get_settings()

OpenLeaf exception hierarchy.

Provides domain-specific exceptions for clear error handling and debugging. All OpenLeaf exceptions inherit from OpenLeafError for easy catching.

Exception hierarchy: OpenLeafError ├── ConfigurationError - Configuration/setup issues ├── ModelError - Model-related errors │ ├── ModelNotFoundError - Aircraft model not available │ └── ModelDataError - Invalid model data ├── ParsingError - Data file parsing errors │ ├── BADA3ParseError - BADA3-specific parsing │ └── BADA4ParseError - BADA4-specific parsing ├── ValidationError - Input/output validation errors │ ├── MissingFieldError - Required field missing from KeyedData │ └── ValueRangeError - Value outside valid range └── EnvelopeError - Flight envelope violations

class BADA3ParseError(ParsingError):
    """Raised when BADA3 OPF/APF file parsing fails.

    Attributes:
        section: OPF section where error occurred (e.g., "AERO", "FUEL").
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        filepath: str | None = None,
        section: str | None = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(message, filepath)
        self.section = section

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        base = Exception.__str__(self)
        parts = [base]
        if self.filepath:
            parts.append(f"file: {self.filepath}")
        if self.section:
            parts.append(f"section: {self.section}")
        if len(parts) > 1:
            return f"{parts[0]} ({', '.join(parts[1:])})"
        return base

class MissingFieldError(ValidationError):
    """Raised when a required field is missing from KeyedData.

    This error provides a helpful message indicating which field
    is missing and which method requires it.

    Attributes:
        field: Name of the missing field.
        method: Name of the method that requires the field.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        field: str,
        method: str | None = None,
        message: str | None = None,
    ):
        if message is None:
            if method:
                message = f"Required field '{field}' missing from data (needed by {method})"
            else:
                message = f"Required field '{field}' missing from data"
        super().__init__(message)
        self.field = field
        self.method = method

    such as OPF, XML, or configuration files.

        self,
        message: str,
        filepath: str | None = None,
        line_number: int | None = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.filepath = filepath
        self.line_number = line_number

        base = super().__str__()
        if self.filepath and self.line_number:
            return f"{base} (file: {self.filepath}, line: {self.line_number})"
        elif self.filepath:
            return f"{base} (file: {self.filepath})"
        return base

class ValueRangeError(ValidationError):
    """Raised when a value is outside its valid range.

    Attributes:
        field: Name of the field with invalid value.
        value: The invalid value.
        min_value: Minimum allowed value (if applicable).
        max_value: Maximum allowed value (if applicable).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        field: str,
        value: float,
        min_value: float | None = None,
        max_value: float | None = None,
        message: str | None = None,
    ):
        if message is None:
            if min_value is not None and max_value is not None:
                message = f"'{field}' value {value} outside range [{min_value}, {max_value}]"
            elif min_value is not None:
                message = f"'{field}' value {value} below minimum {min_value}"
            elif max_value is not None:
                message = f"'{field}' value {value} above maximum {max_value}"
            else:
                message = f"'{field}' value {value} is invalid"
        super().__init__(message)
        self.field = field
        self.value = value
        self.min_value = min_value

docs.text:
Structured logging for OpenLeaf using structlog.

Provides structured, contextual logging for the library with configurable verbosity, without touching global logging state: importing openleaf never calls structlog.configure() nor logging.basicConfig(), so host applications keep full control of their own logging.

Behavior: - If the host application has configured structlog (structlog.is_configured()), OpenLeaf loggers flow through the application's pipeline untouched. - Otherwise, OpenLeaf loggers use a private, library-scoped pipeline writing to stderr, filtered at WARNING by default (override with the OPENLEAF_LOG_LEVEL environment variable or configure_logging()).

Usage: from openleaf.performance.logging import get_logger, configure_logging

Text Only
# Get a logger for your module
logger = get_logger(__name__)
logger.debug("Loading model", aircraft="A320", source="BADA4")
logger.info("Computation complete", duration=0.5)
logger.warning("Value exceeds limit", value=350, limit=340)

# Enable debug logging (affects OpenLeaf's own loggers only)
configure_logging(level="DEBUG")

# Or use environment variable
# OPENLEAF_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG python your_script.py

docs.text:
Configure OpenLeaf's library-scoped logging.

This adjusts only OpenLeaf's own loggers. It deliberately does NOT call structlog.configure() or logging.basicConfig() — a library must not reconfigure the host application's logging. If your application has configured structlog globally, OpenLeaf loggers use the application's pipeline and this function only records the requested level for the fallback pipeline.

Args: level: Log level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL) or None to use environment variable or default. json_format: If True, output logs as JSON (useful for log aggregation). If False (default), use human-readable console output. colors: Whether to use colors in console output. If None, auto-detect based on terminal capabilities.

Example: >>> configure_logging(level="DEBUG") >>> configure_logging(level="INFO", json_format=True)

Source code in packages/openleaf-performance/src/openleaf/performance/logging.py Python
def configure_logging(
    level: str | int | None = None,
    json_format: bool = False,
    colors: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Configure OpenLeaf's library-scoped logging.

    This adjusts only OpenLeaf's own loggers. It deliberately does NOT call
    ``structlog.configure()`` or ``logging.basicConfig()`` — a library must
    not reconfigure the host application's logging. If your application has
    configured structlog globally, OpenLeaf loggers use the application's
    pipeline and this function only records the requested level for the
    fallback pipeline.

    Args:
        level: Log level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL) or None
            to use environment variable or default.
        json_format: If True, output logs as JSON (useful for log aggregation).
            If False (default), use human-readable console output.
        colors: Whether to use colors in console output. If None, auto-detect
            based on terminal capabilities.

    Example:
        >>> configure_logging(level="DEBUG")
        >>> configure_logging(level="INFO", json_format=True)
    """
    if level is None:
        _state["level"] = _get_log_level()
    elif isinstance(level, str):
        _state["level"] = getattr(logging, level.upper(), logging.WARNING)
    else:
        _state["level"] = level

    _state["json_format"] = json_format
    _state["colors"] = colors
    _state["renderer"] = None  # rebuild lazily with the new settings

Get a structured logger for OpenLeaf modules.

Returns a structlog bound logger with optional initial context. If the host application has configured structlog, the application's pipeline is used; otherwise a library-scoped stderr pipeline (WARNING by default).

Args: name: Logger name. Typically name of the calling module. If None, returns the root OpenLeaf logger. **initial_context: Initial context to bind to the logger.

Returns: Configured structlog bound logger instance.

Example: >>> logger = get_logger(name) >>> logger.debug("Loading model data") >>> logger.info("Model loaded", aircraft="A320", source="BADA4") >>> logger.warning("Value exceeds VMO", value=350, vmo=340)

def get_logger(name: str | None = None, **initial_context: Any) -> Any:
    """Get a structured logger for OpenLeaf modules.

    Returns a structlog bound logger with optional initial context. If the
    host application has configured structlog, the application's pipeline is
    used; otherwise a library-scoped stderr pipeline (WARNING by default).

    Args:
        name: Logger name. Typically __name__ of the calling module.
            If None, returns the root OpenLeaf logger.
        **initial_context: Initial context to bind to the logger.

    Returns:
        Configured structlog bound logger instance.

    Example:
        >>> logger = get_logger(__name__)
        >>> logger.debug("Loading model data")
        >>> logger.info("Model loaded", aircraft="A320", source="BADA4")
        >>> logger.warning("Value exceeds VMO", value=350, vmo=340)

        # With initial context
        >>> logger = get_logger(__name__, aircraft="A320")
        >>> logger.info("Computing drag")  # aircraft="A320" included automatically
    """
    if name is None:
        name = _LOGGER_NAME
    elif not name.startswith(_LOGGER_NAME):
        name = f"{_LOGGER_NAME}.{name}"

    if structlog.is_configured():
        # Respect the application's structlog configuration.
        logger = structlog.get_logger(name)
    else:
        # Library-scoped fallback: never touches global structlog/stdlib state.
        logger = structlog.wrap_logger(
            structlog.PrintLogger(file=sys.stderr),
            processors=_PROCESSORS,
        ).bind(logger=name)

    if initial_context:
        logger = logger.bind(**initial_context)

    return logger

Bases: IntEnum

Unified aerodynamic configuration across all models.

These configurations represent discrete flight phases with different aerodynamic characteristics (flap/gear settings).

Uses IntEnum for array API compatibility - values can be used directly in np.where and other array operations.

BADA3 Manual Section 3.5 defines altitude thresholds: - TO: Take-off (up to 400 ft AGL in climb) - IC: Initial Climb (400-2000 ft AGL in climb) - CR: Cruise (above 2000 ft climb, above 8000 ft descent, or fast descent) - AP: Approach (below 8000 ft descent when V < Vmin_CR + 10 kt) - LD: Landing (below 3000 ft descent when V < Vmin_AP + 10 kt)

BADA4 Manual Section 6 uses similar logic with aircraft-specific thresholds.

Source code in packages/openleaf-performance/src/openleaf/performance/core/types.py Python
class AerodynamicConfig(IntEnum):
    """Unified aerodynamic configuration across all models.

    These configurations represent discrete flight phases with different
    aerodynamic characteristics (flap/gear settings).

    Uses IntEnum for array API compatibility - values can be used directly
    in np.where and other array operations.

    BADA3 Manual Section 3.5 defines altitude thresholds:
        - TO: Take-off (up to 400 ft AGL in climb)
        - IC: Initial Climb (400-2000 ft AGL in climb)
        - CR: Cruise (above 2000 ft climb, above 8000 ft descent, or fast descent)
        - AP: Approach (below 8000 ft descent when V < Vmin_CR + 10 kt)
        - LD: Landing (below 3000 ft descent when V < Vmin_AP + 10 kt)

    BADA4 Manual Section 6 uses similar logic with aircraft-specific thresholds.
    """

    TO = 1  # Take-off
    IC = 2  # Initial Climb
    CR = 3  # Cruise (clean)
    AP = 4  # Approach
    LD = 5  # Landing

    @classmethod
    def from_string(cls, name: str) -> AerodynamicConfig:
        """Create from string name (for XML/OPF parsing compatibility).

        Args:
            name: Configuration name ("TO", "IC", "CR", "AP", "LD").

        Returns:
            Corresponding AerodynamicConfig enum value.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If name is not a valid configuration.
        """
        try:
            return cls[name]
        except KeyError:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown aerodynamic configuration: {name}") from None

docs.text:
Bases: ABC

Abstract base class for aircraft performance models.

Combines engine and aerodynamic models to provide complete aircraft performance characteristics.

Source code in packages/openleaf-performance/src/openleaf/performance/core/perfos.py Python
class AircraftModel(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for aircraft performance models.

    Combines engine and aerodynamic models to provide complete aircraft
    performance characteristics.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        data: AircraftData,
        engine: EngineModel,
        aerodynamics: AerodynamicsModel,
        limits: LimitsModel,
    ):
        """Initialize aircraft model with data and subsystems.

        Args:
            data: Aircraft data containing specifications.
            engine: Engine model for thrust and fuel flow calculations.
            aerodynamics: Aerodynamic model for drag calculations.
            limits: Aircraft mass, speed and altitude limits (vmo, mmo, hmo).
        """
        self.data = data
        self.engine = engine
        self.aerodynamics = aerodynamics
        self.limits = limits

    # Abstract init from file
    @classmethod
    @abstractmethod
    def from_file(cls, file: str, **kwargs: Any) -> AircraftModel:
        """Load aircraft model from file.

        Args:
            file: Path to aircraft data file.
            **kwargs: Additional arguments passed to the parser.

        Returns:
            Initialized aircraft model.
        """

    # Quick access to basic data
    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """Aircraft model name."""
        return self.data.model

    @property
    def wtc(self) -> str:
        """Wake turbulence category."""
        return self.data.wtc

    @property
    def engine_type(self) -> EngineType:
        """Type of engine (jet, turboprop, or piston)."""
        return self.data.engine_type

    @property
    def vmo(self) -> float:
        """Maximum operating speed in knots."""
        return self.limits.vmo

    @property
    def hmo(self) -> float:
        """Maximum operating altitude in feet."""
        return self.limits.hmo

    @property
    def mmo(self) -> float:
        """Maximum operating Mach number."""
        return self.limits.mmo

    @property
    def oem(self) -> float:
        """Operating empty mass in kilograms."""
        return self.limits.oem

    @property
    def mtom(self) -> float:
        """Maximum takeoff mass in kilograms."""
        return self.limits.mtom

    @property
    def mpl(self) -> float:
        """Maximum payload mass in kilograms."""
        return self.limits.mpl

    @property
    def surface_area(self) -> float:
        """Wing reference area in square meters."""
        return self.aerodynamics.surface_area

    # --- Abstract Methods ---

    def high_lift(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike | None:
        """Determine high-lift device setting from flight state.

        Returns the current flap/slat configuration. The return type and
        semantics are model-dependent, reflecting each model's native
        representation:

        - BADA4: HLid string from parsed XML AeroConfSchedule (e.g., "0", "1").
                 Raises ValueError if AeroConfSchedule not available in XML.
        - BADA3: Returns None. BADA3 OPF/APF files do not define HLid.
                 Use aerodynamic_configuration() for BADA3-specific data.
        - OpenAP: Flap angle in degrees (0, 5, or 20).
        - PS: Returns 0 (cruise-only model, no high-lift modeling).

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            High-lift device setting (scalar or array), or None if not modeled.
        """
        return None

    def landing_gear(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Determine landing gear state from flight state.

        Default implementation returns False (gear retracted).
        Model-specific behavior:

        - BADA4: Boolean from parsed XML AeroConfSchedule LG mapping.
        - BADA3: Boolean derived from aerodynamic configuration (True = LD).
        - OpenAP: Boolean based on altitude and descent conditions.
        - PS: Returns False (cruise-only, gear always retracted).

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Boolean (True = gear extended, False = retracted).
        """
        return False

    def aerodynamic_configuration(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike | None:
        """Determine aerodynamic configuration from flight state.

        Default implementation returns None (cruise-only or not modeled).
        This enables trajectory simulation with the flow:
            altitude/speed → configuration → hlid/gear → drag_coef

        Model-specific behavior:
        - BADA3: AerodynamicConfig enum based on altitude and speed thresholds
        - BADA4: AerodynamicConfig enum from ARPM configuration schedule
        - OpenAP: String config name based on flight phase detection
        - PS: None (cruise-only model, no configuration rules)

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary containing:
                - altitude: Altitude [m] or altitude_agl for ground-relative
                - calibrated_airspeed or true_airspeed: Speed [m/s or kt]
                - aircraft_mass: Mass for stall speed calculation [kg]
                - flight_phase: Optional flight phase hint

        Returns:
            AerodynamicConfig enum, string, or None if not modeled.
        """
        return None

    # --- Core Performance Methods (KeyedData interface) ---

    def lift_coef(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Calculate lift coefficient from flight state.

        Uses aero.lift_coefficient with aircraft wing area.

        Args:
            data: Flight state dictionary with keys:
                - aircraft_mass: Aircraft mass [kg]
                - true_airspeed: True airspeed [m/s]
                - air_density: Air density [kg/m³]
                - load_factor: Load factor [-] (optional, default 1.0)

        Returns:
            Lift coefficient (dimensionless).
        """
        mass = data["aircraft_mass"]
        v = data["true_airspeed"]
        rho = data["air_density"]
        load_factor = data.get("load_factor", 1.0)

        q = aero.dynamic_pressure(v, rho)
        lift = mass * isa.G * load_factor

        return aero.aerodynamic_coefficient(lift, q, self.aerodynamics.surface_area)

    def lift_coef_from_inputs(
        self,
        v: ArrayScalarLike,
        m: ArrayScalarLike,
        sigma: ArrayScalarLike,
        load_factor: ArrayScalarLike = 1.0,
    ) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Calculate lift coefficient from explicit inputs.

        Convenience method using air density ratio (sigma) instead of density.

        Args:
            v: True airspeed [m/s]
            m: Aircraft mass [kg]
            sigma: Air density ratio (rho/rho_SL) [-]
            load_factor: Load factor [-] (default 1.0)

        Returns:
            Lift coefficient (dimensionless).
        """
        rho = sigma * isa.RHO_SL  # Convert to actual density
        q = aero.dynamic_pressure(v, rho)
        lift = m * isa.G * load_factor

        return aero.aerodynamic_coefficient(lift, q, self.aerodynamics.surface_area)

    def drag_from_inputs(
        self, v: ArrayScalarLike, sigma: ArrayScalarLike, cd: ArrayScalarLike
    ) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Calculate drag force from explicit inputs.

        Convenience method using air density ratio (sigma) instead of density.

        Args:
            v: True airspeed [m/s]
            sigma: Air density ratio (rho/rho_SL) [-]
            cd: Drag coefficient [-]

        Returns:
            Drag force [N].
        """
        rho = sigma * isa.RHO_SL  # Convert to actual density
        q = aero.dynamic_pressure(v, rho)

        return aero.aerodynamic_force(cd, q, self.aerodynamics.surface_area)

    def drag(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Calculate aerodynamic drag force from flight state.

        Uses aero.aerodynamic_drag with aircraft wing area.

        Args:
            data: Flight state dictionary with keys:
                - drag_coef: Drag coefficient [-]
                - true_airspeed: True airspeed [m/s]
                - air_density: Air density [kg/m³]

        Returns:
            Drag force [N].
        """
        cd = data["drag_coef"]
        v = data["true_airspeed"]
        rho = data["air_density"]

        q = aero.dynamic_pressure(v, rho)

        return aero.aerodynamic_force(cd, q, self.aerodynamics.surface_area)

    def thrust_required(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Calculate required thrust for flight condition.

        Uses aero.thrust_required with energy share factor formulation.

        Args:
            data: Flight state dictionary with keys:
                - drag: Drag force [N]
                - aircraft_mass: Aircraft mass [kg]
                - true_airspeed: True airspeed [m/s]
                - vertical_speed: Rate of climb [m/s]
                - f: Energy share factor [-]

        Returns:
            Required thrust [N].
        """
        drag = data["drag"]
        mass = data["aircraft_mass"]
        v = data["true_airspeed"]
        vs = data["vertical_speed"]
        f = data["f"]

        return aero.thrust_required(drag, mass, v, vs, f)

    # --- Limits Delegation Methods ---
    def min_mach(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get minimum mach number.

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Minimum calibrated airspeed in knots.
        """
        return self.limits.min_mach(data)

    def min_cas(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get minimum calibrated airspeed.

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Minimum calibrated airspeed in knots.
        """
        return self.limits.min_cas(data)

    def max_cas(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get maximum calibrated airspeed.

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Maximum calibrated airspeed in knots.
        """
        return self.limits.max_cas(data)

    def max_mach(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get maximum Mach number.

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Maximum Mach number.
        """
        return self.limits.max_mach(data)

    def max_altitude(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get maximum operating altitude.

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Maximum operating altitude in feet.
        """
        return self.limits.max_altitude(data)

    # --- Aerodynamics Delegation Methods ---

    def drag_coef(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Calculate drag coefficient from flight state.

        Delegates to self.aerodynamics.drag_coef(data).

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Drag coefficient (dimensionless).
        """
        return self.aerodynamics.drag_coef(data)

    # --- Engine Delegation Methods ---

    def thrust_min(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get minimum available thrust.

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Minimum thrust in N.
        """
        return self.engine.thrust_min(data)

    def thrust_max(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get maximum available thrust.

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Maximum thrust in N.
        """
        return self.engine.thrust_max(data)

    def fuel_flow(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get fuel flow at current thrust.

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary including thrust.

        Returns:
            Fuel flow rate in kg/s.
        """
        return self.engine.fuel_flow(data)

    def fuel_flow_min(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get minimum fuel flow.

        Args:
            data: Flight state data dictionary.

        Returns:
            Minimum fuel flow rate in kg/s.
        """
        return self.engine.fuel_flow_min(data)

def lift_coef(self, data: KeyedData) -> ArrayScalarLike:
    """Calculate lift coefficient from flight state.

    Uses aero.lift_coefficient with aircraft wing area.

    Args:
        data: Flight state dictionary with keys:
            - aircraft_mass: Aircraft mass [kg]
            - true_airspeed: True airspeed [m/s]
            - air_density: Air density [kg/m³]
            - load_factor: Load factor [-] (optional, default 1.0)

    Returns:
        Lift coefficient (dimensionless).
    """
    mass = data["aircraft_mass"]
    v = data["true_airspeed"]
    rho = data["air_density"]
    load_factor = data.get("load_factor", 1.0)

    q = aero.dynamic_pressure(v, rho)
    lift = mass * isa.G * load_factor

    return aero.aerodynamic_coefficient(lift, q, self.aerodynamics.surface_area)

Trajectory with aircraft model attached - adds performance properties.

This class wraps a TrajectoryData and adds aircraft-specific computed properties like drag, thrust, and fuel_flow.

All TrajectoryData properties are accessible via delegation.

Args: envelope_mode: How to handle flight envelope violations: - IGNORE (default): Compute violations but take no action - WARN: Log warnings when violations are detected - RAISE: Raise EnvelopeViolationError when violations exist

Source code in packages/openleaf-performance/src/openleaf/performance/core/trajectory.py Python
class AircraftTrajectoryData(FlightStateMixin, PerformanceMixin):
    """Trajectory with aircraft model attached - adds performance properties.

    This class wraps a TrajectoryData and adds aircraft-specific computed
    properties like drag, thrust, and fuel_flow.

    All TrajectoryData properties are accessible via delegation.

    Args:
        envelope_mode: How to handle flight envelope violations:
            - IGNORE (default): Compute violations but take no action
            - WARN: Log warnings when violations are detected
            - RAISE: Raise EnvelopeViolationError when violations exist
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        trajectory: TrajectoryData,
        model: AircraftModel,
        envelope_mode: EnvelopeMode = EnvelopeMode.IGNORE,
    ):
        """Initialize with trajectory and aircraft model.

        Args:
            trajectory: TrajectoryData instance.
            model: Aircraft performance model.
            envelope_mode: How to handle envelope violations (default: IGNORE).
        """
        self._traj = trajectory
        self._model = model
        self._envelope_mode = envelope_mode

    def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Get column or computed property from trajectory or aircraft.

        Lookup order:
        1. Input data (trajectory._data)
        2. TrajectoryData computed properties (air_temperature, mach_number, etc.)
        3. AircraftTrajectoryData computed properties (drag_coef, thrust, etc.)
        """
        # Check input data first
        if key in self._traj._data:
            return self._traj._data[key]

        # Check TrajectoryData computed properties
        if key in self._traj:
            return self._traj[key]

        # Check our cached_property
        attr = getattr(type(self), key, None)
        if isinstance(attr, cached_property):
            return getattr(self, key)

        raise KeyError(f"Key '{key}' not found in data or computed properties")

    def __contains__(self, key: str) -> bool:
        """Check if key is available in input data or TrajectoryData.

        NOTE: This does NOT include AircraftTrajectoryData computed properties
        (drag_coef, thrust, etc.) to allow models to distinguish "user provided
        this value" from "system will compute this value on access".
        """
        # Only report keys that are in the input data or TrajectoryData
        # Do NOT include our computed properties - those are outputs, not inputs
        return key in self._traj

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Return number of data points in the trajectory."""
        return len(self._traj)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Return string representation."""
        n = len(self)
        model_name = self._model.model
        model_type = type(self._model).__name__
        return f"AircraftTrajectoryData(n={n}, model={model_name!r}, type={model_type})"

    def __iter__(self):
        """Iterate over input data keys."""
        return iter(self._traj)

    def keys(self):
        """Return input data column keys."""
        return self._traj.keys()

    def get(self, key: str, default: ArrayScalarLike | None = None) -> ArrayScalarLike | None:
        """Get a value by key with optional default.

        Args:
            key: Key to retrieve.
            default: Default value if key not found.

        Returns:
            Value for key or default.
        """
        try:
            return self[key]
        except KeyError:
            return default

    @property
    def data(self) -> dict:
        """Raw input data dictionary from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.data

    @property
    def attrs(self) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
        """Metadata dictionary from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.attrs

    @property
    def trajectory(self) -> TrajectoryData:
        """Access the underlying TrajectoryData."""
        return self._traj

    @property
    def model(self) -> AircraftModel:
        """Access the aircraft model."""
        return self._model

    # ---- Delegated properties from TrajectoryData ----

    @property
    def air_temperature(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Air temperature [K] from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.air_temperature

    @property
    def air_pressure(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Air pressure [Pa] from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.air_pressure

    @property
    def air_density(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Air density [kg/m³] from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.air_density

    @property
    def mach_number(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Mach number [-] from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.mach_number

    @property
    def calibrated_airspeed(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Calibrated airspeed [m/s] from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.calibrated_airspeed

    @property
    def vertical_speed_geometric(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Geometric vertical speed [m/s] from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.vertical_speed_geometric

    @property
    def f(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Energy share factor [-] from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.f

    @property
    def acceleration(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Longitudinal acceleration [m/s²] from trajectory."""
        return self._traj.acceleration

    # ---- Flight envelope (delegated to EnvelopeChecker) ----

    @cached_property
    def _envelope_checker(self) -> EnvelopeChecker:
        """Lazily create the EnvelopeChecker with converted flight state."""
        return EnvelopeChecker(
            model=self._model,
            flight_state=self,
            envelope_mode=self._envelope_mode,
        )

    @property
    def cas_kt(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Calibrated airspeed in knots (for EnvelopeChecker protocol)."""
        from openleaf.performance.physics.units import MS_TO_KT

        return self.calibrated_airspeed * MS_TO_KT

    @property
    def altitude_ft(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Pressure altitude in feet (for EnvelopeChecker protocol)."""
        from openleaf.performance.physics.units import M_TO_FT

        return self._traj["altitude"] * M_TO_FT

    @property
    def mass(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Aircraft mass in kg (for EnvelopeChecker protocol)."""
        return self.aircraft_mass

    @property
    def mach(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Mach number (for EnvelopeChecker protocol)."""
        return self.mach_number

    @cached_property
    def max_cas(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Maximum calibrated airspeed [kt]."""
        return self._envelope_checker.max_cas

    @cached_property
    def min_cas(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Minimum calibrated airspeed (stall speed) [kt]."""
        return self._envelope_checker.min_cas

    @cached_property
    def max_mach(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Maximum Mach number [-]."""
        return self._envelope_checker.max_mach

    @cached_property
    def max_altitude(self) -> ArrayScalarLike:
        """Maximum operating altitude [ft]."""
        return self._envelope_checker.max_altitude

    @property
    def envelope_mode(self) -> EnvelopeMode:
        """Current envelope violation handling mode."""
        return self._envelope_checker.envelope_mode

    @cached_property
    def envelope_violations(self) -> dict[str, ArrayScalarLike]:
        """Detect flight envelope violations (pure computation, no side effects).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with violation flags.
        """
        return self._envelope_checker.envelope_violations

    def check_envelope(self) -> dict[str, ArrayScalarLike]:
        """Check envelope violations and handle according to envelope_mode.

        Returns:
            Dictionary with violation flags.

        Raises:
            EnvelopeViolationError: If envelope_mode is RAISE and violations exist.
        """
        return self._envelope_checker.check_envelope()

    # Check our cached_property
    attr = getattr(type(self), key, None)
    if isinstance(attr, cached_property):
        return getattr(self, key)

Values: IGNORE: Do nothing, just compute values (default). Violations can be queried via the envelope_violations property. class EnvelopeMode(Enum):
    """How to handle flight envelope violations.

    Used by AircraftTrajectoryData to control behavior when trajectory
    points exceed aircraft limits (overspeed, underspeed, ceiling, mass).

    Values:
        IGNORE: Do nothing, just compute values (default). Violations can
            be queried via the envelope_violations property.
        WARN: Log a warning message for each violation type detected,
            but continue computing values.
        RAISE: Raise an EnvelopeViolationError when any violation is detected.
            This happens on first access to envelope_violations property.

    Example:
        >>> perf = AircraftTrajectoryData(traj, model, envelope_mode=EnvelopeMode.WARN)
        >>> _ = perf.envelope_violations  # Logs warnings if violations exist
    """

    IGNORE = "ignore"
    WARN = "warn"
    RAISE = "raise"

class EnvelopeViolationError(EnvelopeError):
    """Raised when flight envelope violations are detected in a trajectory.

    This exception is raised when EnvelopeMode.RAISE is set and the
    trajectory contains points that exceed aircraft limits. Unlike
    EnvelopeError which handles single-point violations, this handles
    batch/trajectory violations with arrays of violation flags.

    Attributes:
        violations: Dictionary mapping violation type to boolean array.

    Example:
        >>> try:
        ...     _ = perf.envelope_violations
        ... except EnvelopeViolationError as e:
        ...     print(f"Violations: {e.violations.keys()}")
    """

        """Initialize with message and violations dict.

        Args:
            message: Human-readable description of violations.
            violations: Dictionary mapping violation type to boolean array.
        """
        super().__init__(message)
        self.violations = violations

class ModelFactory:
    """Unified factory for loading aircraft performance models.

    Provides a consistent interface for loading models from different
    sources without requiring knowledge of the specific model classes.

    Attributes:
        _model_classes: Mapping from ModelType to model class (lazy-loaded).
    """

    _model_classes: dict[ModelType, ModelConstructor] | None = None

    @classmethod
    def _get_model_classes(cls) -> dict[ModelType, ModelConstructor | None]:
        """Lazy-load model classes to avoid circular imports.

        Returns:
            Dictionary mapping ModelType to model class (or None if unavailable).
        """
        if cls._model_classes is None:
            # Import here to avoid circular imports
            # Models may fail to import if their data paths aren't configured
            cls._model_classes = {}

            try:
                from openleaf.performance.models.bada3 import BADA3Model

                cls._model_classes[ModelType.BADA3] = BADA3Model
            except (ImportError, OpenLeafError) as e:
                _logger.debug("BADA3 model not available: %s", e)
                cls._model_classes[ModelType.BADA3] = None

            try:
                from openleaf.performance.models.bada4 import BADA4Model

                cls._model_classes[ModelType.BADA4] = BADA4Model
            except (ImportError, OpenLeafError) as e:
                _logger.debug("BADA4 model not available: %s", e)
                cls._model_classes[ModelType.BADA4] = None

            try:
                from openleaf.performance.models.openap import OpenAPModel

                cls._model_classes[ModelType.OPENAP] = OpenAPModel
            except (ImportError, OpenLeafError) as e:
                _logger.debug("OpenAP model not available: %s", e)
                cls._model_classes[ModelType.OPENAP] = None

            try:
                from openleaf.performance.models.ps import PSModel

                cls._model_classes[ModelType.PS] = PSModel
            except (ImportError, OpenLeafError) as e:
                _logger.debug("PS model not available: %s", e)
                cls._model_classes[ModelType.PS] = None

        return cls._model_classes

    @staticmethod
    def _resolve_model_type(
        model_type: str | ModelType | None,
    ) -> ModelType | None:
        """Convert a string model type to ModelType enum with validation."""
        if not isinstance(model_type, str):
            return model_type
        try:
            return ModelType(model_type.lower())
        except ValueError as e:
            valid_types = [t.value for t in ModelType]
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid model_type '{model_type}'. Valid types are: {valid_types}"
            ) from e

    @classmethod
    def _auto_detect(
        cls,
        icao: str,
        model_classes: dict[ModelType, ModelConstructor | None],
    ) -> AircraftModel:
        """Try each model type in priority order, return first success."""
        errors: list[str] = []
        for mtype in _MODEL_PRIORITY:
            model_class = model_classes[mtype]
            if model_class is None:
                errors.append(f"{mtype.value}: Model not available (not configured)")
                continue
            try:
                return model_class(icao)
            except (KeyError, FileNotFoundError, ValueError, OpenLeafError) as e:
                errors.append(f"{mtype.value}: {e}")

        raise ValueError(
            f"Aircraft '{icao}' not found in any model. Tried:\n"
            + "\n".join(f"  - {err}" for err in errors)
        )

    @classmethod
    def load(
        cls,
        icao: str,
        model_type: str | ModelType | None = None,
    ) -> AircraftModel:
        """Load an aircraft model by ICAO code.

        If model_type is not specified, tries to load models in priority order
        (BADA4 > BADA3 > OpenAP > PS) and returns the first successful load.

        Args:
            icao: ICAO aircraft type code (e.g., "A320", "B738").
            model_type: Specific model type to load, or None for auto-detect.
                Can be a string ("bada3", "bada4", "openap", "ps") or ModelType enum.

        Returns:
            Loaded aircraft model implementing AircraftModel interface.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If model_type is invalid or aircraft not found in any model.

        Example:
            >>> model = ModelFactory.load("A320")
            >>> model = ModelFactory.load("A320", model_type="bada4")
            >>> model = ModelFactory.load("A320", model_type=ModelType.BADA4)
        """
        model_classes = cls._get_model_classes()

        cls,
        file_path: str | Path,

        Args:
            file_path: Path to the model data file.

        Example:
            >>> model = ModelFactory.load_from_file("/path/to/A320.xml", "bada4")
            >>> model = ModelFactory.load_from_file("/path/to/A320.opf", "bada3")
        """
        model_classes = cls._get_model_classes()

        # Convert string to ModelType if needed
        if isinstance(model_type, str):
            try:
                model_type = ModelType(model_type.lower())
            except ValueError as e:
                valid_types = [t.value for t in ModelType]
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Invalid model_type '{model_type}'. Valid types are: {valid_types}"
                ) from e

        model_class = model_classes[model_type]

        if model_class is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Model type '{model_type.value}' is not available. "
                f"Check that the required data path is configured."
            )

        # Use from_file class method if available
        if hasattr(model_class, "from_file"):

        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Model type '{model_type.value}' does not support loading from file."
            )

    @classmethod
    def available_aircraft(
        cls,
        model_type: str | ModelType | None = None,
    ) -> dict[ModelType, list[str]] | list[str]:
        """List available aircraft for one or all model types.

        Args:
            model_type: Specific model type, or None for all types.

        Returns:
            If model_type specified: List of ICAO codes for that model type.
            If model_type is None: Dictionary mapping ModelType to list of ICAO codes.

        Example:
            >>> all_aircraft = ModelFactory.available_aircraft()
            >>> bada4_aircraft = ModelFactory.available_aircraft("bada4")
        """
        model_classes = cls._get_model_classes()

        # Convert string to ModelType if needed
        if isinstance(model_type, str):
            try:
                model_type = ModelType(model_type.lower())
            except ValueError as e:
                valid_types = [t.value for t in ModelType]
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Invalid model_type '{model_type}'. Valid types are: {valid_types}"
                ) from e

        def _get_aircraft_list(mtype: ModelType) -> list[str]:
            """Get aircraft list for a model type, handling errors."""
            model_class = model_classes[mtype]
            if model_class is None:
                return []
            if hasattr(model_class, "available_aircraft"):
                try:
                    return model_class.available_aircraft()
                except (ImportError, OSError, OpenLeafError) as e:
                    # ImportError: optional backend library (openap/pycontrails)
                    # not installed — same contract as unconfigured BADA paths.
                    _logger.debug("Failed to get aircraft list for %s: %s", mtype, e)
                    return []
            return []

        if model_type is not None:
            return _get_aircraft_list(model_type)

        # Return all model types
        return {mtype: _get_aircraft_list(mtype) for mtype in ModelType}

    @classmethod
    def is_available(
        cls,
        icao: str,
        model_type: str | ModelType | None = None,
    ) -> bool | dict[ModelType, bool]:
        """Check if an aircraft is available in one or all model types.

        Args:
            icao: ICAO aircraft type code.
            model_type: Specific model type, or None for all types.

        Returns:
            If model_type specified: True if aircraft available in that model.
            If model_type is None: Dictionary mapping ModelType to availability.

        Example:
            >>> ModelFactory.is_available("A320")
            {ModelType.BADA3: True, ModelType.BADA4: True, ...}
            >>> ModelFactory.is_available("A320", "bada4")
            True
        """
        all_aircraft = cls.available_aircraft(model_type)

        if isinstance(all_aircraft, list):
            return icao in all_aircraft

        return {mtype: icao in aircraft for mtype, aircraft in all_aircraft.items()}
